subject: Business Models
title: Monthly Recurring Revenue
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Monthly Recurring Revenue.

hook.text: If 1,000 customers pay $50/month, your MRR is $50,000. Simple math, powerful insight.

buildup.text: Monthly Recurring Revenue is the heartbeat of subscription businesses. It reveals growth trajectory instantly.

discovery.text: MRR breaks into new MRR (new customers), expansion MRR (upgrades), and churned MRR (cancellations).

twist.text: A company can add customers while MRR shrinks—if downgrades and churn outpace new signups.

climax.text: MRR is the North Star metric. Investors, boards, and operators use it to gauge business health instantly.

punchline.text: Know your MRR, know your future. It's the subscription's pulse.

quiz.question: What three components make up MRR?
options: New MRR, expansion MRR, churned MRR

details.summary: Monthly recurring revenue is the total predictable revenue a subscription business earns each month from active subscribers. MRR is the foundational metric for SaaS and subscription companies because it measures the baseline revenue that will repeat without any new sales effort.
details.whyItMatters: MRR is the metric that defines subscription business health. Investors, operators, and acquirers all evaluate subscription businesses primarily through MRR growth because it represents the compounding revenue engine that drives long-term value.
takeaways: MRR measures total monthly revenue from active recurring subscriptions
Growth in MRR compounds over time as new subscriptions add to the base
MRR breakdown reveals expansion, contraction, and churn dynamics

faq.question: What are the components of MRR that operators track?
faq.answer: New MRR from first-time subscribers, expansion MRR from upgrades and add-ons, contraction MRR from downgrades, and churned MRR from cancellations. Net new MRR equals new plus expansion minus contraction minus churn. Healthy businesses grow net new MRR every month.

faq.question: How is MRR used to value subscription businesses?
faq.answer: Annual recurring revenue, which equals MRR multiplied by twelve, is the primary valuation input. SaaS companies typically trade at 5-20 times ARR depending on growth rate, retention, and margins. A business with $1M MRR and strong growth might be valued at $120M to $240M.
